entries.claim: `closeOver` compares `%cI` timestamps as strings, but ISO-8601 strings with different UTC offsets do not sort chronologically. This can attach an unresolved commit to no close or to the wrong milestone.
entries.failure_scenario: Create a commit dated `2026-01-01T00:30:00+00:00`, then a pruning close dated `2026-01-01T00:00:00-01:00`. The close is actually later (01:00Z), so it should cover the commit, but `p.date >= when` is false lexicographically because `00:00` sorts before `00:30`. `/cad-why` consequently emits “no close has pruned this commit yet” and omits the milestone/archive residue despite a later close existing.

counter_evidence.note: The claim is correct and the code is as described: closeOver at why-corpus.mjs:806 compares %cI strings with >=, and two commits written under different UTC offsets do not string-sort chronologically. Ruled low rather than medium on reachability, not on correctness. Three conditions must hold together: the repository has commits at differing UTC offsets, it has been through a --mode delete close so the pruned-milestone recovery path runs at all, and the mis-ordered pair straddles a prune commit. The consequence is a mislabeled milestone on one /cad-why entry, not a wrong commit or a lost record. Queued as an open item with its fix named: compare Date.parse(p.date) >= Date.parse(when) with a guard for an unparseable date, and pin a mixed-offset pair in why-corpus.test.mjs.
